params.body:
The site addresses the visitor as **u** (u, uw), never je, jij, jou, jouw or jullie. The site enforces this in its own code with a test (ShaneDeconinck/schoutteet, branch `workbench/address-u`). The texts an editor writes here are not in that code, so the Studio now shows the rule and warns.

## What changes

- **Every long text (`localeText`):** the Dutch input carries the hint "Spreek de bezoeker aan met u en uw, nooit met je, jij, jouw of jullie."
- **FAQ question (`faqItem.question`):** shows how to phrase one: as the visitor asks it, "Kan ik ...?", not "Doen jullie ...?".
- **Every Dutch input (`localeString` and `localeText`):** a warning when one of those words appears as a whole word, e.g. `Spreek de bezoeker aan met u en uw. Hier staat "jullie".` It is a warning, not an error, so it never blocks publishing.

The check lives in `schemaTypes/objects/formalAddress.ts`. No field names change, so the content contract (CONTRACT.md) stays as it is.

## Checks

- `npm test`: 13 passed (including the new `tests/formalAddress.test.ts`)
- `npx eslint .` and `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `npx sanity build`: built

After merge the Studio needs a deploy (`npx sanity deploy` with a Deploy Studio token) before editors see the hint.
params.title: Dutch text fields: address the visitor as "u", with a warning
